title: Infinitesimal points and their canonical Lie equivalence over an arbitrary base
statement: Let $S$ be an arbitrary scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $G,H$ be group objects in schemes over $S$, with multiplication, identity and inverse satisfying the group-scheme diagrams of [def-sc-group-scheme], now over $S$. Write $e_G:S\to G$ for the identity section. Let $S[\epsilon]\to S$ be the dual-number thickening: it has underlying space $|S|$ and structure sheaf $\mathcal O_S[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$, using the dual numbers of [def-sc-dual-numbers], with projection $p$ and zero section $i:S\to S[\epsilon]$. Regard this projection as an object of schemes over $S$ (\texttt{dualNumbersOver}). Define the subgroup of infinitesimal points by $\operatorname{Inf}_S(G)=\ker(G(S[\epsilon])\xrightarrow{i^*}G(S))$ (\texttt{infPoints}); thus its elements are morphisms $v:S[\epsilon]\to G$ over $S$ with $v\circ i=e_G$. With $\Omega^1_{G/S}$ as in [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], the identity-cotangent realization of the Lie construction [def-wf-lie-algebra-derivation] is $\operatorname{Lie}_S(G)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_S}(e_G^*\Omega^1_{G/S},\mathcal O_S)$. Define its canonical equivalence $\operatorname{Inf}_S(G)\simeq\operatorname{Lie}_S(G)$ (\texttt{lieEquiv}) by taking the $\epsilon$-coefficient: locally $v^\sharp(a)=e_G^\sharp(a)+\epsilon D_v(a)$ and $v$ is sent to the morphism corresponding to the relative derivation $D_v$. For every group-scheme homomorphism $f:G\to H$ over $S$, define $\operatorname{Inf}_S(f):\operatorname{Inf}_S(G)\to\operatorname{Inf}_S(H)$ (\texttt{infPointsMap}) as the group homomorphism $v\mapsto f\circ v$. No smoothness, affineness, finite-presentation, reducedness, connectedness or characteristic hypothesis is imposed.
